text:
Hail growth
Environment: inside a thunderstorm
Process: supercooled droplets collide with a hailstone and freeze onto it
provenance: Concise factual data extracted from the cited source. Source: NOAA National Severe Storms Laboratory, Hail Basics; https://www.nssl.noaa.gov/education/svrwx101/hail/. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text:
Hailstone layers
Cloudy ice: rapid freezing traps air bubbles
Clearer ice: slower freezing lets bubbles escape
provenance: Concise factual data extracted from the cited source. Source: NOAA National Severe Storms Laboratory, Hail Basics; https://www.nssl.noaa.gov/education/svrwx101/hail/. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text:
Hail fall
Trigger: the updraft can no longer support the stone
Causes: hailstone growth or weakening updraft
provenance: Concise factual data extracted from the cited source. Source: NOAA National Severe Storms Laboratory, Hail Basics; https://www.nssl.noaa.gov/education/svrwx101/hail/. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text:
Wind-driven hail
Fall direction: angled, sometimes nearly sideways in strong winds
provenance: Concise factual data extracted from the cited source. Source: NOAA National Severe Storms Laboratory, Hail Basics; https://www.nssl.noaa.gov/education/svrwx101/hail/. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text:
Hailstone layering
Controls: temperature, liquid-water content, horizontal motion
Layer count: not a count of vertical trips through a storm
provenance: Concise factual data extracted from the cited source. Source: NOAA National Severe Storms Laboratory, Hail Basics; https://www.nssl.noaa.gov/education/svrwx101/hail/. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text:
Melting hail
Formation: high in a thunderstorm
Descent: may melt before reaching the ground
provenance: Concise factual data extracted from the cited source. Source: NOAA National Severe Storms Laboratory, Thunderstorm FAQ; https://www.nssl.noaa.gov/education/svrwx101/thunderstorms/faq/. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text:
Hoar Frost
The deposition of hoar frost is similar to the process by which dew is formed, except that the temperature of the frosted object must be below freezing. It forms when air with a dew point below freezing is brought to saturation by cooling.
— National Weather Service, Glossary

text:
Ice Crystals
A barely visible crystalline form of ice that has the shape of needles, columns or plates. Ice crystals are so small that they seem to be suspended in air. Ice crystals occur at very low temperatures in a stable atmosphere.
— National Weather Service, Glossary

Ice Pellets
pellets of ice composed of frozen or mostly frozen raindrops or refrozen partially melted snowflakes. These pellets of ice usually bounce after hitting the ground or other hard surfaces.

text:
Lake Effect Snow
Snow showers that are created when cold, dry air passes over a large warmer lake, such as one of the Great Lakes, and picks up moisture and heat.

text:
Orographic Precipitation
Precipitation which is caused by hills or mountain ranges deflecting the moisture-laden air masses upward, causing them to cool and precipitate their moisture.
— National Weather Service, Glossary

Rain Shadow

Rime Ice

Snow Pellets

Virga

text:
Supercooled Liquid Water
In the atmosphere, liquid water can survive at temperatures colder than 0 degrees Celsius; many vigorous storms contain large amounts of supercooled liquid water at cold temperatures. Important in the formation of graupel and hail.
— National Weather Service, Glossary
